title: Winspace Agile Review: Sleek, Comfy, Lively but...

takeaways.text: He says the size M is inconsistent with the other sizes, with a lower bottom bracket, shorter chainstays and a relatively short head tube.
Inside, the frame was smooth and well made except for a visible, rough seatstay-to-seat-tube joint; the build had no routing or tolerance problems.
It is much more comfortable than his R12, which has a stiffer rear end, and feels livelier; he notes that his large frame may flex more than smaller sizes.
His complete build weighs about 7.8 kg with power-meter pedals, roughly 300 g less than his R12 with the same wheels and tires.
It fits tires up to 32 mm; he is running 28 mm for now.
The T47 bottom bracket's narrow flanges make the tool easy to slip, and the tapered thru-axles often stick during wheel changes.
The frameset cost US$1,980 without the integrated bar, which adds US$290; he notes the T500 aero frame was US$400 cheaper a few years earlier.

disclosure: Winspace supplied the frame, handlebar and wheels; he paid for the rest of the build and uses a discount code.
summary: A 2,000 km review of a size-L Winspace Agile with Ultegra Di2, compared with his previous Yoeleo R12.
